messages.subject: Implementing Laplace approximation in C++
parts:
Hi, I am trying to apply Laplace approximation to the log-likelihoods.  My intention is to do apply the approximation to individual likelihoods rather than the joint likelihood. However, I am getting an error saying "autodiffr_lap_a.cpp:123:11: error: too many initializers for 'model' ".   Below is my code.  I would appreciate any help regarding this problem. Thanks very much in advance. 

#include <TMB.hpp>

template <class Type>
Type lla(vector<Type> eta_row, vector<Type> dfcost_row, Type rep){
 
  vector<Type> pi_i = exp(eta_row)/(1+exp(eta_row));
  Type l_a = 0;
  for(int h=0; h<rep; h++){
    if(dfcost_row(h) > 0){
      l_a += log(pi_i(h));
    }
    if(dfcost_row(h) == 0){
      l_a += log(1-pi_i(h));
    }
  }
  return l_a;
}  



typedef TMBad::ad_aug ad;
struct model {
  vector<ad> eta_row, dfcost_row; // Data
  ad rep, logsigma_a;
 
  ad operator()(vector<ad> a1) {
   
    ad nll = -dnorm(a1,ad(0),logsigma_a, true).sum();
    nll -= lla(eta_row,dfcost_row,rep);
    return nll;
  }
  template<class Type>
  Type eval_nldens() {
    vector<Type> start(2); start.setZero();
    newton::newton_config cfg;
    Type res = newton::Laplace(*this, start, cfg);
    return res;
  }
};


// Joint likelihood  
template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
 
  /* Data */
  DATA_MATRIX(Xrow);
  DATA_INTEGER(N);
  DATA_VECTOR(replicates);
  DATA_MATRIX(dfcost);
  DATA_INTEGER(maxrep);
 
  /* Parameters */  
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(a1);
  PARAMETER(logsigma_a);
  PARAMETER(alpha0);
  PARAMETER(alpha1);

 
  /* Joint likelihood */
 
  Type nll = Type(0.0);
 
  matrix<Type> eta(N,maxrep);
 
 
  for(int i=0; i<N; i++){
    Type rep = replicates(i);
    for(int j=0; j<rep; j++){
      eta(i,j) = Xrow(i,j)*alpha1 + alpha0 + a1(i);
     
    }
   
  }  
 
  //the joint negative log-likelihood
  for(int i=0; i<N; i++){
   
    vector<Type> eta_row = eta.row(i);
    vector<Type> dfcost_row = dfcost.row(i);
    Type rep = replicates(i);
   
    model obj = {eta_row, dfcost_row, rep, logsigma_a, a1(i)}; // put data vectors here
    nll -= obj.eval_nldens<Type>();}
  return nll;
}

parts:
The error says that the random effect initialization here:
vector<Type> start(2); start.setZero();
is invalid (returns non finite inner value or gradient). Note that this could be caused by something else such as invalid outer parameters or an error in your objective function implementation.

You may want to track what's going on in the inner problem by setting
    newton::newton_config cfg;
    cfg.trace=true;

BTW, the config parameters are documented here: https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/structnewton_1_1newton__config.html

However, your manual implementation will only provide the second term (J*V(theta)*t(J)) representing the standard delta method applied on the random effect modes. I don't have an easy workaround to give the full uncertainty.
